The two accent edges B–D and C–D form a smallest edge cut, so the adhesion (edge connectivity) is 2. The card shows that cut and the value 2." width="100%"} The adhesion is the minimum number of edges whose removal would disconnect the graph. Also called edge connectivity. Only defined for undirected graphs. Returns `0` if already disconnected. This is an alias for `edge_connectivity()` that additionally rejects directed graphs. Adhesion is a single-number summary of how robust a network is to link failures: a graph with adhesion `k` stays connected after any `k - 1` edges are removed. Typical uses include comparing the fault tolerance of alternative network designs and checking that a network has no single critical link (adhesion of at least `2`). Adhesion is never larger than the minimum node degree, since removing all edges of the least-connected node isolates it. Edge weights are ignored; every edge counts as one. Graphs with fewer than two nodes, or that are already disconnected, return `0`. Use `cohesion()` for the node-based counterpart, `minimum_cut_value()` for a specific pair of nodes, and `bridges()` to list the edges whose individual removal disconnects the graph. The method does not modify the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Minimum edge cut size: the smallest number of edges whose removal disconnects the graph. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is directed. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a 4-cycle, every node has degree 2, so at least 2 edges must be removed to disconnect it: ::: {#c356c7ce .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A")]) ) graph.adhesion() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Adding the two diagonals turns the cycle into the complete graph `K_4`, where every node has degree 3 and the adhesion rises to 3: ::: {#c1075aa5 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.add_edge("A", "C").add_edge("B", "D") graph.adhesion() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: A path has a single link holding each part together, and a graph made of two separate pieces is already disconnected: ::: {#03d737cb .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(4) two_pieces = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(2).add_path_graph(2) path.adhesion(), two_pieces.adhesion() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (1, 0) ``` ::: :::
